article.story: LOS ANGELES -- — Alijah Arenas scored 21 points, Rodney Rice added 18 and No. 21 Southern California routed Arkansas-Pine Bluff 122-46 on Sunday. The Trojans (4-0) won by 76 points to set a program record for margin of victory against a collegiate opponent, breaking the previous record of 64 against New Mexico in 1955. USC also had 66-point wins against Manual Arts High School in 1913 and Southern California Telephone in 1925. It was the second time this week the Golden Lions (0-5) were on the wrong side of a record-setting margin of victory. No. 9 UCLA had a 69-point win over Arkansas-Pine Bluff on Wednesday. USC’s 122 points tied its second-most in school history, matching a Dec. 21, 1970, showing against Alabama. The Trojans had 130 points against Meiji in 1962. Adonis Ratliff had 17 points and eight rebounds, helping USC get off to a comfortable start by scoring 10 of its first 17 points. USC shot 64.7% (22 of 34) from the field and had 16 assists to three turnovers in the first half, taking a 62-19 lead into the break. USC ended up making 44 of 67 attempts (65.7%) with a school-record 35 assists. Freshman power forward Christian Collins, a five-star recruit from Inglewood, California, made his USC debut. He had two points, two assists, two blocks and a steal in 12 minutes. He was on a minutes restriction coming off an undisclosed injury, coach Eric Musselman said. Jai’chaunn Hayes and Jahmari Hamilton-Brown each had 11 points for Arkansas-Pine Bluff, which lost its three-game road swing against UCLA, Cal Baptist and USC by a combined 159 points. The Golden Lions, who have given up at least 106 points in all four of their games to Power 4 opposition, face six more road contests before their home opener against Ecclesia College on Dec. 16. Up next Arkansas-Pine Bluff: At Arkansas State on Wednesday night. USC: Hosts Tarleton State on Thursday night. ------ Sign up for Top 25 poll alerts here, visit the Top 25 here and see AP’s full men’s basketball coverage here
